NOVELTY STATEMENT — The standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE using porosity optimization and nickel particle size distribution to accommodate volume changes. My same-class mechanism departure is a graded porosity architecture with controlled pore formers that create a stress-relief buffer zone at the anode-electrolyte interface. This addresses the failure physics by providing controlled void volume to accommodate nickel expansion without transmitting stress to the brittle electrolyte interface.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the volumetric expansion coefficient of nickel (α_Ni ≈ 4.5×10^-5 K^-1) and the maximum tolerable strain in YSZ (ε_YSZ ≈ 0.2%). For a 200°C temperature swing during start/stop, ΔT = 200°C, the expected strain in nickel is ε_Ni = α_Ni × ΔT = 9×10^-3. The graded porosity must accommodate this expansion while limiting interfacial strain to <0.2%. CALCULATED: A porosity gradient from 40% (electrolyte side) to 25% (gas channel side) provides ~15% void volume, sufficient to absorb the 0.9% volume change without significant stress transmission.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
- Anode support layer: NiO-YSZ composite with graded pore formers (same class as standard practice's NiO-YSZ)
  - Pore former: PMMA microspheres (off-the-shelf, same class as standard practice's pore formers)
    - Size distribution: 2-8 μm (graded) at electrolyte interface to 10-20 μm at gas channel
  - Binder: Same polyvinyl butyral (PVB) as standard practice
- Processing: Same tape casting and co-firing parameters as standard practice (no new equipment)
- Sintering profile: Same temperature range (1350-1400°C) with modified hold time to achieve porosity gradient (same thermal budget as standard)
- No new instrumentation required (uses existing quality control systems)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: SAME - same thickness (2 mm), same electrical connections, same sealing requirements
- Operability: SAME - operates at same temperature (750°C), same fuel gas composition, same voltage range
- Maintenance: SAME - requires same inspection protocols, same replacement procedure
- Rough cost: SAME - materials are same class, processing is same with minor modification, no new capital equipment
- The graded pore former distribution requires more precise mixing control but uses existing mixing equipment

EXECUTABLE TEST:
- Protocol: Subject 5 test cells to 200 thermal cycles between 750°C (operating) and room temperature (shutdown) with 1-hour holds at each temperature. Measure power density at 0.7V after every 20 cycles. Perform post-mortem SEM/EDS analysis of anode microstructure and interface.
- Instruments: Standard test station with temperature control, voltage/current measurement, SEM/EDS analysis system
- Pass/fail threshold: Power density must remain ≥0.35 W/cm² after 200 cycles; no visible cracks or delamination at anode-electrolyte interface
- Duration: ~2 weeks (including analysis)
- Kill criterion: Power density drops below 0.35 W/cm² at any point; or visual inspection reveals cracks/delamination before completing 200 cycles
